examples.text: Я приехала к очень серьёзному человеку. Он меня ждёт.
examples.trans: I have come to see a very important man. He is waiting for me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: conferring or showing high social status

examples.text: Он купил себе дорогие статусные часы.
examples.trans: He bought himself an expensive status watch.

examples.text: Костик, ты дурак! Это статусная вещь.
examples.trans: Kostik, you're a fool! This is a status piece.

meanings.note: сто пятьдесят = a hundred and fifty; сто рублей = a hundred roubles

examples.trans: I've got a hundred and ten.

examples.text: Понимаешь, Аркаша, мы все скидываемся на этот кластер. Мне москвичам сегодня надо отдать сто пятьдесят.
examples.trans: You see, Arkasha, we're all chipping in for this cluster. I have to give the Moscow people a hundred and fifty today.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Core Russian pron meaning 'such, like this' in everyday speech.
Person who lacks courage. Common masculine noun meaning 'coward' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да потому что ты трус, Костик!
examples.trans: That's because you're a coward, Kostik!
I am not a coward at all!

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Possession. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.
Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to see, to catch sight of
meanings.note: Вот увидишь! = you'll see!. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'видеть'.

examples.text: И Нину свою ты больше не увидишь!
examples.trans: And you'll never see your Nina again!

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money
Хватит!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be enough', paired with 'хватать'.

examples.trans: Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: plural-only noun: эти часы = this watch
Plural of час. Common substantive noun meaning 'watch, clock' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Видишь эти часы? Это швейцарское золото.
examples.trans: See this watch? It's Swiss gold.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Я что-то вижу = I see something. Core Russian pron meaning 'something; somehow' in everyday speech.
colloquial, used as an adverb: что-то я не вижу = somehow I don't see it
pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!
